thread_text:
anya: quick heads-up — ran a focused sweep comparing streaming handshake overhead vs non-streaming completions for microbatch sizing. short tl;dr: streaming p95 prefers smaller mb (1-2) but p99 spikes from kernel warmup + KV cold misses. details below.

sam: nice, you have numbers? link? :eyes:

anya: dashboard + raw traces: https://redwood-infer/p/exp/handshake-prefetch-171234 (internal)
summary: 
- streaming (mb=1): p50 28ms, p95 110ms, p99 420ms
- streaming (mb=2): p50 35ms, p95 95ms, p99 260ms
- streaming (mb=4): p50 60ms, p95 140ms, p99 700ms
- non-stream (sync batch mb=8): p50 40ms, p95 160ms, p99 320ms
(note: ms per-request end-to-end on c6g-gpu-xx, mixed chat/completions traffic synthetic)

devon: wow p99 700ms at mb=4 for streaming. is that KV miss tail or kernel selection?

anya: traced a sample of p99 tails: ~60% kernel switch + JIT-like fallback (we call it "slow-kernel" path), ~30% KV cold miss causing extra KV fetch roundtrip, ~10% other (GC, network retries).

lucas: can you paste the config you used?

anya: config snippet we used:
```
model: gptx-1.3b
mode: streaming
microbatch_sizes: [1,2,4,8]
kernel_hint: auto
kv_prefetch_enabled: false
warmup_rounds: 0
metrics: p50,p95,p99,tail-cause
```

taylor: interesting that enabling larger mb increases p99 for streaming. guess: larger mb forces different kernel (vectorized path) that has higher tail variance on short sequences because of tail-work scheduling?

sam: maybe the kernel chooser is using throughput-optimized kernels at mb>=4 which have higher cold-start latency. we should check kernel selection histogram.

anya: yep. kernel histogram shows kernel_variant=A (fast, throughput) at mb>=4; kernel_variant=B (latency-optimized) at mb<=2. A has better steady throughput but much heavier warm path when first chosen (cache misses for fused kernels).

lucas: can we force `kernel_hint: prefer-latency` in runtime to test?

anya: did that in a follow-up: forcing latency kernels for mb=4 drops p99 from 700ms -> 210ms but p50 goes up 60ms -> 85ms, p95 slightly better. So tradeoff is clear.

perf-ci: benchmark run complete: run id=exp-171234-02, artifacts @ s3://perf/exp-171234-02 (internal).

devon: what about KV prefetch? enabling it might hide the KV cold miss portion.

anya: toggled kv_prefetch_enabled=true for mb=4: p99 improved from 700ms -> 380ms (still worse than mb=2). Combine kv_prefetch + prefer-latency kernel -> p99 ~200-230ms. That seems acceptable but steady throughput drops ~12%.

taylor: so actionables: for streaming chat we should bias default mb to 2, enable kv_prefetch short window, and prefer latency kernels during handshake. For non-stream completions we can keep mb higher for throughput.

sam: agree. also consider hysteresis/handshake window: when a client opens a streaming session we should keep a short sticky kernel_hint for that connection for first N requests to avoid repeated warmups.

lucas: good point — add `handshake_sticky_hint_ms` config, maybe default 10s. avoids flip-flopping kernel selection for bursty clients.

anya: proposed rollout plan: 
1) canary runtime with `streaming_defaults: {mb:2, kv_prefetch:true, kernel_hint:prefer-latency, handshake_sticky_hint_ms:10000}` on 5% infra for 48h
2) collect p50/p95/p99 + kernel choice histogram + KV hit rate and rollback criteria p99 increase >10%
3) if stable, 25% -> 100% over a week.

devon: +1. also add a small A/B on device types (gpu gen X vs Y) because kernel behavior varied across hw.

perf-ci: note: perf artifacts include per-node kernel-switch traces and KV fetch latencies. use `scripts/analyze_tail.py --run exp-171234-02` to reproduce tables.

sam: will you open a PR for the runtime defaults and a k8s canary manifest?

anya: yes, creating PR now: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/PR-402 (WIP). will add perf graphs and rollback knobs.

lucas: thanks — will allocate canary nodes and tag the job.

taylor: small nit: document reasoning in runbook so oncall can understand why streaming uses mb=2 by default. otherwise they might flip it for throughput.

anya: will add a short note in docs/runbooks/streaming-mb.md in the PR.

sam: awesome. last q: any short-term fix for existing clusters without rollout? a quick flag we can toggle?

anya: we can flip `kernel_probe_threshold` to a higher value to avoid early kernel switch in-flight, and enable kv_prefetch globally. both are low-risk and reversible. I'll add them to PR as optional flags for ops to toggle.

devon: :thumbsup: thanks for running this. saved us from a surprise tail after the last throughput tweak.

anya: np — will post a final summary after the 5% canary starts.

sam: thanks everyone.
